title: Railway proof workflow reported success before runtime admission was safe
affected_scope: isolated UX Cycle 10 r3 proof service only

timeline.event: Railway accepted the exact branch upload and created deployment c61f470f-bb51-4ed0-afcd-1ecce926ecb6.
Runtime began failing with EACCES while attempting to create /app/local-data under the deliberately read-only application tree.
GitHub Actions had already completed the deployment proof job successfully even though Railway runtime logs were failing.

A bounded redeploy started in development-mode semantics instead of hosted-staging semantics and emitted a demo credential into the platform log stream. The credential value is intentionally not recorded here.
A subsequent redeploy started with hosted-staging semantics on the expected public bind/port and reached Railway SUCCESS.

root_cause.primary: The isolated proof workflow treated a successful Railway CLI --ci upload/build result as sufficient deployment evidence instead of independently proving the deployment reached a safe terminal runtime state.
contributing: The isolated service was created without the canonical proof-service healthcheck/restart configuration.
The workflow did not validate required hosted-staging variables before upload.
The immutable /app boundary correctly rejected the fallback local-data path, but the failure was not part of the CI admission oracle.
The runtime retained a development fallback capable of logging demo authentication material when hosted-staging configuration was incomplete.

permanent_prevention_rules: Any workflow that invokes railway up must validate the hosted-staging variable contract before upload.
A Railway upload/build acknowledgement must never be treated as runtime success; poll deployment status to a terminal state.
After terminal SUCCESS, assert /api/health and expected staging identity before claiming proof completion.
Root-directory deployments must not use an unnecessary positional dot path in this repository.
No credential value may be written to CI or provider logs, including demo/default credentials.
Isolated proof services should inherit the canonical service baseline: Dockerfile build, /api/health healthcheck, bounded restart policy, and explicit hosted-staging variables.
